text: Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Kustklassieker, 198km along the North Sea coast.
The flag is about to drop. It's dry, 11 degrees, and there is a stiff north-westerly coming off the sea.
Racing is under way and it is frantic from the gun, as you'd expect on a day like this.
Several attacks have already been shut down. Nobody is being allowed an inch.
Ruben Vermeulen and Tomas Bergstrom have a small gap, but Soudal Quick-Step are not letting that one go.
Back together. The elastic snaps again immediately as another six riders try their luck.
This one might be it. A five-man move has gone clear at the front of the race.
In the break: Ruben Vermeulen, Tomas Bergstrom, Callum Wright, Jonas Halvorsen and Pieter Maes.
The peloton sits up and lets them go for now. The gap is 45 seconds.
With 160km to go the advantage is out to 2 minutes and growing.
Our coverage is brought to you by Kustbank. Subscribe to our newsletter for daily race analysis.
Lidl-Trek have put two riders on the front of the bunch. The gap has stabilised at 3'20".
With 140km to go the gap to the five leaders is 3'45". Nobody seems worried yet.
Riders are taking on food from the team cars. A quiet spell in the race.
Photo: the breakaway silhouetted against the dunes. Beautiful stuff from our man on the moto.
With 120km to go the gap is down to 3 minutes. Alpecin-Deceuninck have moved up.
A word of warning — the road turns north at Zeewijk in about 20km, and that means a full crosswind.
The bunch is already lining up single file in anticipation. Positioning is everything now.
Alpecin-Deceuninck and Visma-Lease a Bike are massing on the front. This looks deliberate.
Here we go. They have turned into the wind and the bunch is strung out in the gutter.
Echelons are forming. The front group is fanned right across the road.
There is a split! The first echelon has around 30 riders and the second group is losing ground fast.
With 95km to go, the second group is at 25 seconds and the third at over a minute.
Mathieu Vanden Berghe has missed the split. That is a disaster for Lidl-Trek.
The leaders' advantage has come tumbling down to 1'50" — the echelon behind is flying.
The second group is working hard but they are not organised. The gap has gone out to 50 seconds.
With 78km to go the front echelon of 28 riders leads the second group by 1'10".
The road turns inland and the wind is now a tailwind. The chase behind will find that easier.
Regrouping behind. The second and third groups have come together, about 60 riders now at 1'20".
With 55km to go the five leaders are at 1'15" over the front echelon.
Crash in the front group! Several riders down on a roundabout with 45km to go.
Jonas Halvorsen has been distanced from the breakaway. Four leaders now.
The pace has gone up again. Visma-Lease a Bike have three riders driving with 38km to go.
With 30km to go the gap to the four leaders is down to 55 seconds. This is being closed down.
Callum Wright attacks out of the breakaway! He has gone alone with 24km to go.
Wright has 20 seconds on his former companions and 40 on the chasing group.
The other three escapees have been caught. Only Wright remains out front, 30 seconds clear with 16km to go.
With 12km to go Wright's lead is 18 seconds. He is emptying himself out there.
Alpecin-Deceuninck are lining up on the front. The lead-out is starting to take shape with 9km to go.
Wright is caught with 7km to go. All back together at the head of the race.
Immediate counter-attack from Pieter Maes, but the sprinters' teams are having none of it.
Fighting for position now. Elbows out with 4km to go and the road narrowing.
Alpecin-Deceuninck have four riders in a line at the front with 3km to go.
Under 2km to go. Soudal Quick-Step are trying to come over the top on the left.
Flamme rouge. Alpecin-Deceuninck still have two men ahead of their sprinter.
The sprint is on! Jasper Van Rompuy launches from third wheel.
Van Rompuy wins the Kustklassieker! He held off the fast-finishing Soudal Quick-Step rider by half a length.
Stage result: 1. Jasper Van Rompuy 2. Milos Petrovic 3. Andreas Kohl.
What a race. The crosswind section at Zeewijk decided it — half the peloton never recovered from that split.
